environment.tool: manual audit of the tag source + live compiled binary; scripted strict-token peer that echoes the request line verbatim, a per-request exec counter, and byte-exact client capture

findings.description: cachebase is `"http://"+host+target` with the untouched target, so `%2f`, uppercase hex, a trailing `&` and a trailing slash are all distinct keys for the same decoded resource. 40 of 40 cross-spelling reads re-executed (counter incremented). A client that spells the token differently is not served the attacker's entry. Host casing is normalised and does hit the same key; only the target is raw.
findings.title: The cache keys on the raw target, so every spelling of one resource is a separate entry

limitations: All RCE is RCE on the upstream host
Needs a cache-enabled config and an upstream that sends Cache-Control: public, max-age=
